app.setup.title_default.why: System-settings-style status title, same shape as Apple's own 'Wi-Fi 꺼짐'; plain state, no instruction (button below carries that).

app.setup.title_failed.why: Hedged toward 'could not confirm' rather than 'is off', reads clearly distinct from title_default.

app.setup.detail_default.s: 가드를 켜면 페이지가 탭과 클릭을 가로채지 못합니다.
app.setup.detail_default.back: guard turn-on-if page tap-and-click hijack cannot
app.setup.detail_default.why: Conditional -면 carries the logic instead of a connector word; one plain declarative sentence, the app's whole pitch.

app.setup.detail_failed.s: Safari에서 상태를 확인하지 못했습니다. 확장 프로그램을 켜면 앱이 스스로 알아챕니다.
app.setup.detail_failed.back: Safari-in status could-not-confirm. extension turn-on-if app itself notices.
app.setup.detail_failed.why: Two plain sentences instead of a 하지만-joined one; no error code named, matches the note against surfacing raw system errors.

app.setup.open_button.why: Verb-plus-object button label; '확장 프로그램' is Apple's own term for Safari's Extensions pane, works verbatim on both screens.

app.welcome.heading.why: Warmth carried by the exclamation, not a register switch — kept in 합니다체 like every other string in the file.

app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.tit.why: Native word 막 (thin layer) instead of the loanword 레이어, matching the plain, concrete-noun register the brief asks for.

app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.s: 보이지 않는 막이 화면을 덮어 다른 곳이 대신 눌립니다.
app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.back: not-visible layer screen covers, other spot instead gets-pressed
app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.why: Describes the experience (something else gets pressed) rather than the mechanism, as the brief asks.

app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.title.why: Short, concrete noun phrase naming the trick, no marketing language.

app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.s: 누르는 순간과 떼는 순간 사이에 링크 주소가 바뀝니다.
app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.back: press moment-and release moment between-in link address changes
app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.why: States the timing plainly; no hedge, no 그래서.

app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.ti.why: 불청객 (uninvited guest) is idiomatic Korean and lands the same tone as 'uninvited windows' without sounding like a translated compound.

app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.s: 가드를 켜면 누른 곳으로만 새 탭이 열리고, 다른 것은 끼어들지 않습니다.
app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.back: guard turn-on-if pressed-place-only-to new tab opens, other thing does-not-butt-in
app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.why: Written as the promise the brief asks for, not a description of the trick; one comma joining two clauses of the same event, not a 그리고-chain.

app.welcome.feature.every_destination.ti.why: Names the rule-list feature: everything gets tracked, not only what got caught.

app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.s: 발견된 대상마다 목록에 남아, 이 사이트나 전체에서 허용할지 차단할지 정합니다.
app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.back: found destination-each list-in remains, this site-or whole-in allow-whether block-whether decide
app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.why: One sentence carries both facts (every destination logged, scope choice) without a padded three-item list.

app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.t.why: Literal, concrete match for how guarding is switched on — per site, not automatically.

app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.s: Safari 도구 막대의 Undirect 버튼을 누르면 그 사이트의 가드가 켜집니다.
app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.back: Safari toolbar-of Undirect button press-if that site-of guard turns-on
app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.why: -면 conditional carries the mechanism; '도구 막대' is Apple's own Korean term for toolbar.

app.nav.guarded_sites.why: Compact compound that fits a ~190px sidebar column and reads the same as a nav title; canonical term for 'guarded site' used everywhere in this file.

app.nav.settings.why: Apple's own term for this screen on both iOS and macOS.

app.nav.app_title.why: Proper noun, left untranslated as the brief expects.

app.rules.grouping.everywhere.why: Canonical 'everywhere' scope phrase, reused across app and extension so the two contexts read the same.

app.rules.grouping.by_site.why: Reads as the clear opposite of 모든 사이트 sitting beside it in the sidebar.

app.rules.empty_no_app.title.why: States a wiring/first-contact gap, not 'there is no content' — kept distinct from empty_no_rules.title.

app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.s: Safari에서 아무 페이지나 한 번 열면 자동으로 채워집니다.
app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.back: Safari-in any page-whichever one-time open-if automatically gets-filled
app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.why: One sentence, no setting to change — matches the brief's 'no setting, just normal use of Safari'.

app.rules.empty_no_rules.title.why: Plain two-word contrast to empty_no_app.title: connected to the extension, this particular list is just empty.

app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.s: 대상을 직접 허용하거나 차단해야 목록에 나타납니다.
app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.back: destination directly allow-or block-must-do list-in appears
app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.why: Explains a rule is created only by an explicit decision, not merely by the guard noticing something.

app.rules.footer.lifetime_count.why: Korean carries no plural agreement, so one form covers every count; %lld kept exactly as the SwiftUI placeholder per the notes.

app.rules.row.state_blocked.why: One-word state label, clear opposite of state_allowed.

app.rules.row.state_allowed.why: One-word state label paired with state_blocked.

app.rules.row.action_allow.why: Bare verb-stem menu item, shown only when the row currently reads Blocked.

app.rules.row.action_block.why: Bare verb-stem menu item, shown only when the row currently reads Allowed.

app.rules.row.help_tooltip.why: Describes what the control under the pointer does, in one short declarative sentence.

app.rules.row.use_default.why: Names clearing the explicit rule so the destination falls back to the default policy — deletion, not a new verdict.

app.watched.empty.title.why: Uses the canonical 가드 사이트 term; states plainly that no site has been switched on.

app.watched.empty.detail.s: 문제가 있는 사이트에서 Safari 도구 막대의 Undirect 버튼을 누르세요.
app.watched.empty.detail.back: problem-having site-on Safari toolbar-of Undirect button press
app.watched.empty.detail.why: Names the exact mechanism for guarding a first site, in one sentence.

app.watched.footer.s: 새 사이트는 Safari 도구 막대의 버튼으로만 추가됩니다.
app.watched.footer.back: new site-topic Safari toolbar-of button-only-with gets-added
app.watched.footer.why: Reminds the person this screen only removes, never adds — the toolbar button is the sole source.

app.watched.row.guarded_badge.why: Read-only status word for iOS, parallel to the 가드 사이트 / 가드 중인 사이트 phrasing used elsewhere.

app.watched.row.stop_button.why: Short imperative-shaped verb noun for a trailing row button, matching 'Stop' exactly.

app.watched.row.stop_tooltip.why: States plainly what the Stop button under the pointer does.

app.settings.guard_toggle.why: Canonical one-word term for the master switch, reused as the noun throughout the file.

app.settings.state_on.why: Generic on-state word, reused for both the Guard and page-note rows.

app.settings.state_off.why: Generic off-state word, opposite of state_on.

app.settings.mode_heading.why: Section heading introducing the choice of which sites the guard actually runs on.

app.settings.mode_watched.why: Phrased from the person's own action ('sites you turned on yourself'), as the brief asks, not as a technical mode name.

app.settings.mode_everywhere.why: Contrasts cleanly with mode_watched as the automatic, always-on option.

app.settings.banner_toggle.why: Names the on-page banner toggle, separate from the popup's own record of what happened.

app.settings.policy_heading.why: Introduces the last section: what happens to a destination with no explicit rule at all yet.

app.settings.policy_block.why: Picker option for the stricter default policy.

ext.meta.name.why: Proper noun shown in Safari's extension list; left as-is like any app's own name.

ext.meta.description.s: 페이지가 클릭이나 탭을 가로채 엉뚱한 곳으로 이동시키지 못하게 막습니다.
ext.meta.description.back: page click-or tap hijack wrong place-to move-cause cannot-do blocks
ext.meta.description.why: One explanatory sentence for a first-time reader browsing the extension list, slightly more descriptive than in-app copy as the brief asks.

ext.meta.app_title.why: Fallback display name standing in for a missing site name; same brand word.

ext.toolbar.tooltip_on.why: States plainly that guarding is currently on for the active tab's site.

ext.toolbar.tooltip_off.s: 이 사이트에서 가드 꺼짐 · 눌러서 켜기
ext.toolbar.tooltip_off.back: this site-on guard off · pressing turn-on
ext.toolbar.tooltip_off.why: Middle dot joins state and call-to-action as two noun-form fragments, avoiding a dash and avoiding a register-breaking imperative ending.

ext.toolbar.tooltip_no_site.why: Brief fragment explaining there is nothing to guard on this tab.

ext.popup.no_site_title.why: Heading fragment: Undirect only has something to do on an actual website.

ext.popup.no_site_body.s: 실제 웹사이트를 연 뒤 여기를 누르면 가드가 켜집니다.
ext.popup.no_site_body.back: real website opened after here press-if guard turns-on
ext.popup.no_site_body.why: Conditional -면 replaces an imperative, keeping the declarative register; '여기' keeps the brief's self-reference to the toolbar button the popup hangs off.

ext.popup.watch_switch_label.why: Screen-reader-only label naming exactly what the switch controls, since the visible row already shows the site name.

ext.popup.watch_unknown.why: Explains why the switch is disabled: there is genuinely no page here to guard.

ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.s: 이미 설정에서 모든 사이트를 가드하도록 되어 있습니다.
ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.back: already settings-in every site guard-to set is
ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.why: Explains the switch is redundant because Settings already runs the guard everywhere; ordinary resultative -어 있다, not the banned double passive.

ext.popup.watch_master_off.why: 자체 (itself) makes clear the master switch is off, not this particular site.

ext.popup.watch_on.s: 가드가 켜져 있습니다. 끄면 페이지가 다시 로드됩니다.
ext.popup.watch_on.back: guard is-on. turn-off-if page again loads
ext.popup.watch_on.why: Confirms state then warns of the reload with a -면 conditional, no dash.

ext.popup.watch_off.s: 가드가 꺼져 있습니다. 켜면 페이지가 다시 로드됩니다.
ext.popup.watch_off.back: guard is-off. turn-on-if page again loads
ext.popup.watch_off.why: Direct before/after pair with watch_on, same sentence shape.

ext.popup.page_heading.why: Names the section listing what the current tab specifically reached for, distinct from the site-wide rule lists.

ext.popup.page_off.why: Dead key as of 2026-09-22 per the brief; written speculatively in the same voice as the other page-section states, using -어 causal ending instead of a connector word.

ext.popup.page_quiet.s: 이 페이지에서 다른 사이트로 가려던 시도가 없습니다.
ext.popup.page_quiet.back: this page-on other site-to going-tried attempt none
ext.popup.page_quiet.why: States plainly that nothing on this page has reached for another site so far.

ext.popup.page_empty.why: Dead key, worded around the empty list rather than a quiet page, per the brief's note that it is a near-synonym of page_quiet.

ext.popup.stopped_one.why: Korean carries no singular/plural split, so this and stopped_other share one form; $COUNT$ kept as the extension's own placeholder.

ext.popup.stopped_other.why: Same form as stopped_one — see its note on Korean's lack of plural agreement.

ext.popup.seen_one.why: 'Seen' is broader than 'stopped' (blocked and allowed together); 전체 marks that breadth. Shares one form with seen_other.

ext.popup.seen_other.why: Same form as seen_one — no plural distinction in Korean.

ext.popup.tries_one.why: Per-destination try count, terse enough to sit among the row's other short fragments; identical to tries_other.

ext.popup.tries_other.why: Same form as tries_one — Korean's counter 회 needs no plural variant.

ext.popup.recipe_heading.why: Lead-in fragment meant to read as 'Applied fix: <recipe name>' once concatenated with a colon in code.

ext.state.blocked.why: Same reused word as app.rules.row.state_blocked, so it reads consistently across app and extension.

ext.state.allowed.why: Opposite of state.blocked, reused across rows, menu options and scope phrases.

ext.state.removed.why: Distinct word for a trap taken off the page itself, since there is no destination here to allow or block.

ext.scope.here.why: Leading middle dot lets `${verdict} ${scope}` compose as '차단됨 · 이 사이트' using the template's existing space, without reordering the code.

ext.scope.everywhere.why: Same middle-dot composition as scope.here; canonical 모든 사이트 phrase.

ext.scope.default.why: Composes as '차단됨 · 기본값에 따름' (blocked, following the default), same middle-dot pattern.

ext.action.allow_here.why: Standalone menu option, unambiguous about scope since it is not composed with a separate verdict word.

ext.popup.policy_heading.why: Same phrasing as app.settings.policy_heading so the concept reads identically between app and popup.

ext.policy.block.why: Same wording as app.settings.policy_block, separate translation unit.

ext.popup.bridge_warning.s: 이 페이지의 보안 설정 때문에 가드 일부가 작동하지 않아, 보호가 완전하지 않습니다.
ext.popup.bridge_warning.back: this page-of security settings because-of guard part-not operate, protection complete-not
ext.popup.bridge_warning.why: 때문에 carries the causation as a single grammatical link, not a discourse connector; names the limitation as belonging to this page, not the extension.

ext.kind.click_catcher.why: 함정 (trap) is the native word, avoiding an extra loanword; sits naturally in a comma-joined list of kind tags.

ext.kind.overlay.why: 덮개 (cover) instead of the loanword 오버레이, distinguishing this broader case from the click-catcher tag.

ext.kind.synthetic_click.why: Names a click the page's own script made up, not a real press.

ext.kind.window_open.why: 팝업 is an established, non-inflated loanword for this concept in Korean.

ext.kind.form_submit.why: Names the specific hidden-form-submit trick, distinct from a normal link or window call.

ext.kind.href_swap.why: Names the mid-press destination swap concretely.

ext.kind.back_hijack.why: Names a navigation fired right after the person's own back gesture.

ext.kind.redirect.why: Names the core same-tab-redirect trick this extension exists to stop.

ext.kind.pop_tab.why: Distinguishes a tab-under-style new tab from a normal window.open pop-up.

ext.kind.network_rule.why: Names the earliest, strongest kind of block — stopped before it ever reached the page.

ext.reason.way_back.why: Explains why a redirect was allowed: its own address carries a path back to the original site.

ext.reason.sized.why: Explains why a window was allowed: it asked for a deliberate size, not a bare full tab.

ext.reason.took_press.why: Explains why a destination was blocked: it rode a press aimed at something else.

ext.reason.default_allow.why: Explains an unrated destination went through because nothing said to stop it, so the default policy applied.

ext.reason.own_code.why: Explains a window was allowed because the code opening it belonged to the site itself, not a third party.

ext.popup.rules_link.why: Reused verbatim as the nav row, the Rules screen's own header, and the back-button's accessible label when leaving it.

ext.popup.back_link.why: Accessibility label naming where a chevron-only back button returns to — the popup's main per-page view — reusing the page_heading term for consistency.

ext.rules.everywhere_heading.why: Section heading for rules scoped to every guarded site, same canonical phrase used throughout.

ext.rules.by_site_heading.why: Clear counterpart to everywhere_heading, spelled out with 규칙 since this entry's budget allows a third word.

ext.rules.empty.why: Terse single-row placeholder, same wording as app.rules.empty_no_rules.title.

ext.action.allow.why: Bare menu-item word; scope is already fixed by which section the row sits in.

ext.action.block.why: Bare menu-item word, opposite of allow.

ext.action.clear.why: Same underlying action and wording as app.rules.row.use_default, phrased for the popup's tighter menu.

ext.popup.settings_heading.why: Reused as both the nav row and the settings sub-screen's own header title.

ext.settings.guard_label.why: Same one-word term as app.settings.guard_toggle, used both as the visible row text and the switch's screen-reader label.

ext.settings.guard_on.why: State label for the master switch when on, parallel to app.settings.state_on.

ext.settings.mode_heading.why: Same phrasing as app.settings.mode_heading for the identical concept in the popup.

ext.settings.mode_watched.why: Same wording as app.settings.mode_watched, kept consistent across surfaces.

ext.settings.banner_toggle.why: Shorter than the app-side label to fit the popup's tighter budget, same underlying page-note concept.

ext.action.report.why: Names opening a pre-filled report; the person still has to submit it themselves, so no promise of anything sent automatically.
